files.purpose: Defines the full catalogue of 26 app themes (enum AppTheme) with their display names, detail strings (shown as the Settings Theme row detail for the selected theme) and a private hex palette (fixed color scheme, accent, glass surface tint, success/warning/danger hues), and turns a theme into a ThemeSpec of SwiftUI Colors plus a circular picker swatch view. It also owns ThemeManager, the process-wide static mirror of AppSettings.theme that caches the current ThemeSpec once per theme change and posts the Notification "ThemeManager.didChange" so layer-backed views (spinner cells) can recolor, and a Color(hex:) initializer that parses 6-digit sRGB hex strings with or without a leading '#'.

state_owned: ThemeManager.current: AppTheme, static, default .system, nonisolated(unsafe); doc comment says it is mirrored from AppSettings.theme, which is the source of truth

ThemeManager.spec: ThemeSpec, static, private(set), nonisolated(unsafe), initialised to AppTheme.system.spec and rebuilt in current's didSet (cache so hex parsing is not repeated on every Chrome.accent read)
side_effects: Setting ThemeManager.current rebuilds ThemeManager.spec and posts Notification ThemeManager.didChange (object nil) on NotificationCenter.default, synchronously on the setter's thread. The didSet fires on every assignment, including assigning the same theme again (Swift didSet has no equality check).
No file I/O, no persistence, no network.
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSColor(name: nil, dynamicProvider:) with NSAppearance bestMatch(from: [.darkAqua, .aqua]) == .darkAqua for the .system surface: a Windows port needs a color that re-resolves when the OS light/dark setting changes (e.g. prefers-color-scheme / nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors)
SwiftUI ColorScheme? (.light/.dark/nil = follow system), applied by callers as the preferred color scheme

Color.accentColor: the macOS system control accent; used in the swatch when a theme's accent is nil (system, light, dark), and ThemeSpec.accent stays nil so callers keep the system accent. Windows needs the Windows accent color (e.g. systemPreferences.getAccentColor) or a fixed fallback
System semantic colors .green, .orange, .red used as status fallbacks when palette entries are nil; the port needs the macOS systemGreen/systemOrange/systemRed equivalents per appearance
Color.primary.opacity(0.22) for the swatch rim, which is appearance dependent

Liquid Glass: the header comment states themes tint glass and never paint opaque surfaces; surface is a tint for macOS glass/material backgrounds, which Windows must approximate (Mica/acrylic or translucent CSS)
Foundation Scanner.scanHexInt64 and NotificationCenter; Swift nonisolated(unsafe) statics (unsynchronised globals read on the main thread)
Detail string for .system is "Follows your Mac" (macOS-specific wording)
persisted_fields: AppTheme is Codable with String raw values equal to case names (e.g. "system", "catppuccinMocha", "gruvboxLight", "claudeLight", "matrix"). This file writes nothing; persistence is in AppSettings: UserDefaults key "appTheme" (AppSettings.swift:135 `static let appTheme = "appTheme"`), written in AppSettings.theme didSet as `defaults.set(theme.rawValue, forKey: Key.appTheme)` followed by `ThemeManager.current = theme` (AppSettings.swift:286-290).

Load (AppSettings.init, AppSettings.swift:724-728): `AppTheme(rawValue: defaults.string(forKey: Key.appTheme) ?? "") ?? AppTheme(rawValue: defaults.string(forKey: Key.appearance) ?? "") ?? .system`, so an unknown or missing "appTheme" value falls back to the legacy "appearance" key (AppSettings.swift:137, old System/Light/Dark values "system"/"light"/"dark" map onto the same cases), then to .system. Then `theme = initialTheme` (inside init, so AppSettings.theme didSet does not run) and an explicit `ThemeManager.current = initialTheme`, which runs ThemeManager.current didSet: spec is rebuilt and ThemeManager.didChange is posted once at launch. ThemeManager.current defaults to .system before that.

feature_notes: Header doc lists the themes as Catppuccin, Dracula, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbox, One Dark, Everforest, Kanagawa, Rosé Pine, Solarized, GitHub, Ayu, Night Owl, Monokai, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Matrix, and states that a theme tints the glass and recolors the accent and status hues and never paints opaque surfaces.

spec: for .system the surface is the dynamic NSColor (1E1E20 dark / FFFFFF light); for every other theme surface is Color(hex: palette.surface), so .light is fixed FFFFFF and .dark fixed 1E1E20. accent maps through Color(hex:) or stays nil (nil keeps the system control accent). success/warning/danger fall back to .green/.orange/.red when nil (only system, light and dark have nil status hues).

Palette coincidences to preserve exactly: everforest accent and success both A7C080; rosePine accent and danger both EB6F92; monokai accent and danger both F92672; matrix accent and success both 00E676; nord and cursor share accent 88C0D0; solarizedDark and solarizedLight differ only in scheme and surface; githubDark and codex share success/warning/danger 3FB950/D29922/F85149; claude and claudeLight share accent C15F3C; githubLight and claudeLight share warning 9A6700.

ThemeManager.didChange doc: posted for layer-backed views whose colours are set once rather than resolved on every draw (the spinners' cells). ThemeManager.spec doc: Chrome.accent and friends are read in hundreds of view bodies per frame and building a spec parses hex colors, so the parse is cached per theme change.

Color(hex:): trims whitespace/newlines via .trimmed, drops one leading '#', scans with Scanner.scanHexInt64 into a UInt64 starting at 0; red = (value >> 16) & 0xFF, green = (value >> 8) & 0xFF, blue = value & 0xFF, each divided by 255, opacity 1, color space .sRGB. Error path: the Bool result of scanHexInt64 is ignored and value starts at 0 (line 241 `var value: UInt64 = 0`). Foundation scanHexInt64 scans hex digits up to the first non-hex character and keeps that prefix, so only a string whose first character is not a hex digit (or an empty string) yields 0 (black); "12GG34" gives 0x12 (red 0, green 0, blue 0x12). scanHexInt64 also accepts an optional "0x"/"0X" prefix, and on overflow (more than 16 hex digits) stores UInt64.max, giving white (FFFFFF). A port must reproduce this prefix parse; no shipped palette string exercises it (all are 6-digit literals); an 8-digit string uses only the low 24 bits (last six hex digits); 3-digit forms are not expanded ('FFF' gives red 0, green 0x0F, blue 0xFF).

B1->B2: exactly one line changed, in Color(hex:) at line 239: `var text = hex.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` became `var text = hex.trimmed`. String.trimmed (Core/Support/Text.swift:132) is `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`, so behaviour is identical; no theme, palette, string, swatch or ThemeManager change between 1.6.0 and 1.6.2.
unresolved_questions: How ThemeSpec.surface (Chrome.glassTint) is blended into the glass (opacity/material) is decided by Chrome glass modifiers outside this file; not verified here.

Whether SwiftUI mirrors a LinearGradient with .leading/.trailing unit points under a right-to-left layout direction is framework behaviour not established by the source; moot for the shipped left-to-right, English-only build.
